issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: the template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput), but the problem statement (task description and UML) and the solution implementation define addGuestStudents(int). This parameter-list mismatch (extra boolean parameter in the template) contradicts the exercise specification and will confuse students about the required public API and may cause compilation or test failures when tests or example usage call addGuestStudents with a single int parameter.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the specification and solution: replace the method declaration in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java with public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and implement its body accordingly. If input validation is desired, implement it internally or add a private helper/overload, but keep the public API consistent with the problem statement and solution.

issues.description: The concept is 'add guest students' for the Lecture class. The problem statement and UML/task describe and expect a single-parameter method named addGuestStudents(int) (problem statement: addGuestStudents(int)). The solution implementation defines public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) (solution: addGuestStudents(int)). However, the template starter declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with an extra boolean parameter (template: addGuestStudents(int, boolean)). This mismatched method signature (different parameter list for the same conceptual operation) forces students to reconcile conflicting APIs, may break automated tests that expect the single-parameter signature, and increases cognitive load when mapping the UML/task to the starter code.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and implement the addition behavior there. Remove the extra boolean parameter validateInput from the template. Ensure any template comments or helper code reflect the single-parameter API so tests and students use the same signature.
